notes.kkodi: Called at the door before you enter.
notes.yingira: Taaha, come in: the reply to Hodi!
notes.ennyumba: Enju, a house; omuka, at home.
notes.mpa: Mpa, give me. Add ninkushaba to be polite.

guidebook.intro: Visiting someone’s home has its own little ritual: knock, wait to be invited in, sit and accept a drink. You’ll also name the rooms and ask for things.

tips.title: Hodi! Taaha!
body: Call **Hodi!** at the door. The host answers **Taaha!** (come in) and then **Ikara hansi** (sit down). Guests are told **Nitushemererwa kukureeba**, “we’re glad to see you”.

tips.title: Mpa, ndeetera: asking for things
body: Commands are the bare verb: **Kinga orwigi** (close the door), **Kingura** (open). To ask for something for yourself, add **m-** or **n-**: **Mpa** (give me), **Ndeetera amaizi** (bring me water).
Soften any request with **ninkushaba** (please, literally “I ask you”).

culture.title: A guest is never sent away hungry
body: A visitor is offered something before any talk: milk, tea or a meal. Refusing everything can seem cold, so accept at least a little.
